core.text: Maintain independent registration and recognition counts: six registrations and seven distinct recognitions remain. Registration enables receipt requests but does not itself acknowledge a sender.

Proposed next action: at tick 0 validate N3 and individually request N2. Continue validation N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 1,2,3,4,5. Individually request N3,N4,N5,N6 at ticks 1,2,3,4; idle dispatcher at tick 5; bulk request at tick 6. Model prediction: deliveries N2 through N6 at ticks 1 through 5, then N7 at 7 and N8 at 8; eight registrations and eight recognitions, using six actions. This is a derived schedule, not an observed execution.

Closest rival: use bulk at the same dispatcher ticks 0,1,2,3,4,6 with the same validations. Separating probe: replay both schedules under stipulated transitions; compare boundary-9 registration and distinct-recognition ledgers against queue duplicates and dashboard identities. FIFO calculation predicts rival recognition only N1,N2,N3, versus all eight for the proposed schedule.

Defeat: proposed replay exceeds six actions, misses either eight-count target, or requires a transition absent from the model. Actor burden: registration clerk performs six validations; dispatcher selects five individuals and one bulk request; server runs automatically and ledgers add no clerk labor. Probe checks finite feasibility, without a global-optimality or empirical-performance claim.

residue.text: Inconvenient display residue: N1 is already recognized yet dashboard-pending through boundary 3, clearing at 4. Delay origin is unknown; this establishes no wider defect.

Timing residue: empty initial queue prevents tick-0 delivery. Requests become eligible one boundary later; tick-8 requests cannot contribute. Duplicates and failures consume the same scarce FIFO delivery ticks as first recognitions.

Capacity residue: seven remaining individual receipts need seven actions but only six exist. Bulk combines requests, including every registered pending identity; it adds no server capacity. Extra actions, servers, configuration changes, repairs, channels and clerks are unavailable.

Boundary residue: N8 cannot receive successfully before tick 6. All timings are synthetic fixed stipulations. No new notices arrive. Later sender adaptation and extra status-query demand are unobserved hypotheses; no empirical comparison or globally best schedule proof is supplied.

tension.account_a: Rival hypothesis: routine bulk calls at ticks 0,1,2,3,4,6 suffice despite dashboard lag.
tension.account_b: Selective early requests and a late bulk preserve distinct-delivery opportunities; repeated bulk queues redundant identities.
tension.prediction_a: The rival hypothesis predicts eight recognitions with six bulk calls; the stipulated FIFO replay can defeat it.
tension.prediction_b: With identical validations, selective schedule yields eight recognitions; routine bulk yields three by boundary 9.
